rule: Postgres ownership, visibility and deletion state control access. Authenticate private reads and mutations; revalidate search hits before exposing text or metadata. Client owner IDs and vector payloads are not authority.
Validate uploaded media, paths and request limits. Never interpolate user input into shell commands or expose credentials, private transcripts or signed media URLs to unauthorized callers.

Postgres owns durable work and retry state; Redis is only transport. Commit new job intent with the corresponding state transition. Preserve persisted attempt limits and transactional finalizer creation.
Lease, deadline and processing-token checks fence renewals, publication, completion and failures. S3 paths and Qdrant writes are attempt-specific; obsolete workers cannot replace accepted artifacts.
Upload idempotency keys are owner-scoped and bound to the payload fingerprint. Retries replay the committed response; changed payloads conflict and old tokens cannot commit a replacement reservation.
Schema changes require Alembic migrations and compatibility consideration. Route HTTP behavior belongs in routes; reusable logic belongs in services/repositories.

Keep React/TypeScript and FastAPI response, error and readiness contracts aligned. Preserve optional feature configuration and report degraded or unavailable search separately from successful empty results.

Require focused regression coverage for changed behavior. Tests must use isolated services. Kafka readiness claims require completed evidence for each acceptance gate; admission is not consumer throughput and accepted-event accounting is not zero capture loss.
